package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the SheetJS (xlsx) package contain a vulnerable regular expression that allows for Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attacks. Maliciously crafted input can cause catastrophic backtracking, leading to excessive CPU/memory consumption and potential application DoS.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (during XML parsing of user-supplied Excel files)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This regular expression is used to match XML/HTML tags in user-supplied input. Its structure allows for catastrophic backtracking when processing large, specially crafted input strings.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The regex is overly permissive and complex, making it susceptible to catastrophic backtracking when handling long, repetitive input. This can be exploited to cause a denial of service.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal XML tag parser should use efficient, well-bounded regex or a proper XML parser to avoid ReDoS. Here, the regex can be abused by attackers to freeze or crash the application.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Regex is commonly used for simple tag matching, but not for untrusted, potentially large user input.
key_indicators: No input length or complexity checks

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits a large, specially crafted Excel (XML-formatted) file with repeated character sequences.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggers the vulnerable regex during XML parsing.

attack_chain.action: Regex engine processes the input, causing catastrophic backtracking.
attack_chain.leads_to: Excessive CPU/memory usage, leading to application freeze or crash (DoS).

behavioral_signatures: Use of complex, unbounded regular expressions on user-supplied XML/HTML input
Application CPU/memory spike during parsing of large or repetitive XML files
Unusually long processing times for certain file uploads
file_indicators: bits/75_xlml.js containing the vulnerable xlmlregex assignment
Any JavaScript file with similar regex patterns for XML tag parsing
network_indicators: N/A (attack is local to the application, not network-based)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript source code for complex regular expressions used on user-supplied input, especially in XML/HTML parsing contexts. Monitor application logs and resource usage for spikes during file uploads or parsing. Use static analysis tools to flag regex patterns known to be susceptible to ReDoS. Upgrade to SheetJS version 0.16.0 or above to ensure the vulnerability is patched.
